holderPosition.legalForm: Not established. The older catalogue calls USDY a tokenized yield-bearing note; research found the issuer and the governing issuance terms unresolved after a December 2025 migration: current notes name Ondo Global Markets (BVI), legacy references name Ondo USDY LLC
holderPosition.says: The holder has some claim on an Ondo issuer for a dollar amount that accrues yield from short-term Treasuries and bank deposits, but which entity owes it, under which terms, with what security and in what rank cannot be said for any given token. Holding the token does not by itself meet the issuer's eligibility and onboarding rules for redemption.

chainFacts.says: Classic SPL mint, 6 decimals, supply 156,471,531.738738 USDY on Solana; readable by the /fungible reader.

Mint authority 8n2uiRUd1A9NN78PKESkJe6k6zMqtKCZh3MrK1j9qkB1; freeze authority 51QVCuHfL1FeNjd8BDeffCKhCcAYoULnVB3yjNhShiuK. No permanent delegate, transfer hook or default-frozen accounts, so transfers are not gated by the token program, but any account can be frozen. Who holds the keys is not in the sources.

outside.says: Public materials show both a legacy wire route and a Global Markets USDC route; which applies, its timetable, minimum and fees are unresolved. Stays in the issuance terms of the holder's vintage.
Whether a security agent holds collateral for the holders, any guarantor and the holders' rank on insolvency depend on terms that were not obtained.
rUSDY wraps locked USDY; it is not additional collateral and is a separate instrument.

verdict.summary: The mint is classic SPL, so it is one of the few researched tokens the reader can hold A/H/T for. v3 can also show the real problem: two issuers' token terms for one mint, and a flag. But it cannot say what the claim is (claim kind unknown, security for the holders as a class, rank on insolvency), and which record prevails and who may redeem are only proposals. Most backing and security statements come only from Ondo's own docs as cited by the older catalogue.
